Concept stage · Engineering blueprint v1.0

Collapsible Sky Panel rack
for the Hummer EV eTrunk

A tiered, scissor-lifted rack that holds the four removable Sky Panels flat and isolated when they are off the truck, then folds down to a low deck when the panels are back on, giving the eTrunk back to cargo.

eTrunk volume (total)
11.3 cu ft
Collapsed height target
2.25 in
Panels held
4 one per tier
OEM set MSRP
$795

Feasibility verdict: buildable as a prototype, with six things to fix first

The mechanism is simple statics and well within normal hardware. Loads are low, a few dozen pounds per side. The risks are dimensional, not structural. Everything below is built from your sketches, and every number is tagged as VERIFIED, ASSUMED or MEASURE so you can see what is real.

  • Nothing here is measured yet. The panel dimensions and weight, and the eTrunk interior and hood clearance, are not published anywhere I could find. The earlier draft's 30×25×3 in and 16 lb are placeholders. Your own sketches disagree with each other (40, 36, 28, 45, 25, 18, 16 in). Measure the truck before anything else.
  • "Reclaims 11.3 cu ft" was wrong. 11.3 cu ft is the whole eTrunk. A 32×28×2.25 in deck occupies about 1.2 cu ft, so the real claim is "returns roughly 90% of the volume while the panels are on the truck". Whether that beats OEM depends on whether the OEM trays also nest down (unknown, see Problem).
  • The 2.25 in collapsed height only works with thin plates. The earlier draft specified 1020 T-slot extrusion, which is 1 in tall and would not fold below 4 in. The design needs ~0.19 in formed or ribbed plates and 0.5 in pitch hardware.
  • "Patent-pending" has been removed. Nothing has been filed. Do a prior-art search before using that phrase anywhere.
  • Expect it to be heavier than the OEM trays. The live model puts an aluminum build near 38 lb against 26.81 lb for the OEM package, which matters when you lift it out of the truck.
  • Market is small and the incumbent is cheap. The OEM tray set is $795 MSRP. A hand-built aluminum rack will not beat that on price, so it is a personal build first and a product only if the fold-flat benefit survives a real test.
01 · Problem

Why the OEM trays waste the eTrunk

The factory Sky Panel Storage Set stacks four trays in the eTrunk. That is great for the panels, but the stack takes most of the space whenever it is installed.

What is verified

eTrunk volume11.3 cu ftVERIFIED
OEM set, part no.85841998VERIFIED
OEM set contents4 trays, cover, strapsVERIFIED
OEM package size43.12 × 24.5 × 16.62 inVERIFIED
OEM package weight26.81 lbVERIFIED
OEM MSRP$795VERIFIED
FitmentPickup 2022–26, SUV 2024–26VERIFIED

Source: GMC Accessories product page for the Sky Panel Storage Set for eTrunk (checked Oct 26, 2026). Volume from the Recharged cargo-space article. An older GM Authority post lists the set at $595, so the price has risen.

What the OEM comparison hinges on

The package envelope of 43.12 × 24.5 × 16.62 in is about 10.2 cu ft, close to the whole 11.3 cu ft eTrunk. That is a shipping box, not an installed footprint, but it hints that four loaded trays fill the space.

The package length of 43 in also suggests the panels may be nearer 40×24 in than the 30×25 in assumed earlier.

Open question that decides the project: do the empty OEM trays nest or fold down, and how tall are they empty? If they already collapse to a few inches, your advantage shrinks to convenience and panel isolation. Check this before building. A dealer or an owner forum will know in one reply.

What the renders show that the design must honor: the slatted deck is the load floor in the collapsed view, so it has to carry bags and a backpack, not just hold its own weight. 03 · Design

How the mechanism works

Four platforms, one fixed and three lifted by scissor stages on each side. Each platform carries one panel on its perimeter only.

Structure

  • Base frame bolted or strapped to the eTrunk floor tie-downs
  • Platform 1 fixed to the base at one collapsed pitch
  • Platforms 2–4 ride on three scissor stages per side
  • Pivots at link centers, one slotted pin per stage

Panel support

  • Panels rest only on a perimeter rim, never on the glass center
  • Forward-curved cradle on the nose side matches the panel's curved edge
  • EVA foam strip on the rim, TPU corner saddles
  • Strap or toggle per tier to stop rattle

Lock and fold

  • Spring detent locks the stack at full extension
  • One release folds all three stages together
  • Collapsed latch holds the deck down against bumps
  • Cargo can sit on the deck once collapsed

Design rules the numbers must satisfy

RuleFormula
Expanded pitch between platform topspe = panel rim height + air gap + plate thickness
Collapsed heightHc = base + 4 × collapsed pitch
Loaded stack heightHs = base + pc + 3·pe + panel rim height
Link length must exceed peL > pe, with sin θ = pitch / L
Slider travel per stageL (cos θc − cos θe)
Hood clearanceHs < measured eTrunk depth − margin

06 · Alternatives

Is the scissor rack the right architecture?

Scores are my judgment on a 1–5 scale (5 is best), not measured data. They are meant to help you decide what to prototype first.

OptionBuild effortCollapsed heightPanel safetyReliabilityNotes
A. Scissor-lift rack (your concept)2543Best fold-flat result. Most parts, pinch points, and racking to manage.
B. Hinged flip-up shelves4344Tiers hinge up from a rear spine and rest on side stops. Far fewer parts, but collapsed pile is thicker.
C. Removable nesting trays5345Closest to OEM. Trays nest and the stack leaves the truck, or goes into a cover bag.
D. Slide-out drawer frame3453Panels slide in on rails. Needs the full depth of the eTrunk to extract, awkward with the hood.
Recommendation: prototype B in Coroplast or plywood in one weekend alongside the full-scale panel templates, and keep A as the premium version. If B's collapsed pile is under about 4 in, it may be good enough, and far easier to make and sell.
07 · Bill of materials

Prototype BOM and cost

Rough estimates for one hand-built prototype, not quotes. Prices vary with supplier and region.

PartSpecQtyEst. cost
Platforms6061 aluminum, 0.125–0.19 in, lightened or ribbed4$120–220

Estimated rack weight (aluminum)
—
From the live model at 0.19 in plates, 60% lightened. The OEM package is 26.81 lb, so expect this rack to be heavier. A 0.125 in plate or a composite honeycomb core would help.
Price reality
OEM set is $795 MSRP. A CNC aluminum rack would cost more to make, so a product version would need stamped or laser-cut and bent parts, or a premium positioning.
Branding and IP
Describe fitment as "for Hummer EV" but avoid using GM marks in the product name or logo. Run a patent and design prior-art search before disclosing publicly.
08 · Verification

Test plan

Pass criteria are proposals. Tighten them once real panel weights are known.

TestMethodPass criterion
Static load, extendedLoad platforms with the real panels, plus sandbags to 2× the measured stack weightNo permanent set, no pivot binding, lock holds
Static load, collapsed deck100 lb distributed on the deckDeflection under 0.25 in, no rattle
Fold cycleExtend and collapse 1,000 cycles, then inspectUnder 15 s per fold, no pivot wear or loose hardware
Hood clearanceClose the hood on the loaded stack, using a cardboard stand-in firstAt least 1 in of margin everywhere
Drive test30 min of mixed road with a recorded phone on the rackNo panel movement, no audible rattle
Panel contact checkInspect with a flashlight after each testContact only on the rim, none on the glass
Heat soakParked in Florida sun with a thermometer on the foamNo foam or TPU warping
Finger safetyReview every pinch point during collapseNo gap that closes below 0.5 in near a handle or grab point
09 · Risks

Risk register

RiskLikelihoodImpactMitigation
Real panels are bigger or heavier than assumedHIGHHIGHMeasure before cutting metal. Everything in the model is parametric.
Loaded stack hits the hoodMEDIUMHIGHMeasure depth. If tight, drop to three tiers plus the panel on the truck floor, or use option B.
Scissor racking and rattleMEDIUMMEDIUMTwo link pairs per side, tight pivot tolerance, straps, foam. Test on a drive.
Glass chips from contact during loadingMEDIUMHIGHRim cradles with lead-in guides, EVA at every contact, and a loading procedure printed on the rack.
Pinched fingers in the scissorsMEDIUMMEDIUMSide covers, handle placement away from the pinch zone, a single release.
Rack too heavy to handleMEDIUMMEDIUMThe model puts an aluminum rack at roughly 35–40 lb versus 26.81 lb for the OEM package. Use thinner or honeycomb platforms, and add a carry handle.
Collapsed deck not low enoughMEDIUMMEDIUMProve the 0.5 in pitch on a two-tier test section before building all four.
OEM trays already nest, weakening the benefitMEDIUMHIGHAsk owners and a dealer now. It costs nothing.
Liability if soldUNKNOWNHIGHPersonal build first. Talk to a product-liability insurer before selling.
10 · Roadmap

Build sequence with go / no-go gates

Measure the truck and the panelsFill every MEASURE row in the dimension register. Photograph the eTrunk with a tape measure in frame. Ask owners whether the OEM trays nest.
GATE: loaded stack height fits under the hood with 1 in margin, and the OEM trays do not already solve the problem.
Update the model, pick the architectureEnter the real numbers above. If option B gets close enough, build B first.
Time: 1 evening · Cost: $0
Full-scale Coroplast mockupCut four panel templates, a base, and stacked platforms. Check loading by hand, the hood, and the curved nose edge.
Time: 1 weekend · Cost: about $30–60
Two-tier mechanical proofBuild one scissor stage with the real plate thickness and pivot hardware. Confirm the 0.5 in collapsed pitch and the slider travel.
GATE: collapses to 0.5 in pitch and extends to the pe above with no binding.
Full four-tier prototypeAdd the remaining stages, saddles, cradles, detent lock and straps.
Time: 2–3 weekends · Cost: $360–720
Test planRun the tests above with the real panels. Fix, then repeat the drive test.
GATE: all tests pass with no glass contact.
Decide: keep, refine, or productizeIf selling, do the prior-art search, move to laser-cut and bent parts, get a liability opinion, and price against the $795 OEM set.
